scope: The real launcher (LauncherWindow, SessionWorker, LauncherSession; host and join) with native games and no emulator: a native runtime bundle (the Windows exe and its SDL2.dll, run under Wine; or the Linux executable under the bundle's .exe name with a placeholder SDL2.dll; the launcher's own bundle and installation checks ran either way), production world creation, host enrollment of both legacy saves through bootstrap games that close themselves, the friend's invitation; both launchers start their games, which Continue into the overworld; the host opens Start > Player > Players, picks Battle Friend and Challenge 1v1; the friend opens Pending challenge and accepts; both press Enter battle; default moves until the battle ends, with the forced switch when the host's first Pokemon faints; both launchers report battle_finished with the original game processes, bridges and runtime identities; the durable result is the same for both; each player's full personal party is back in memory; each game's Players > Challenges > Recent battle results shows it; both save through the launcher (revision 2); both games close normally (exit 0: SIGTERM on Linux, Alt+F4 under Wine); fresh launchers Continue onto the same canonical saves; the host store passes its integrity check; source saves unchanged. Ordinary key presses on each player's own X display; the harness reads the games' memory (/proc/PID/mem at the non-PIE executable's symbols) only to see menus, tasks and parties, never writes it.

checks: host enrollment closed each bootstrap game itself (exit 0), revision 1 for both
host and friend launchers started their games; both reached the overworld with save, window, battle and menu capabilities, terminal savers armed, save leases held
challenge, acceptance and Enter battle through the Players menu on both games; both consent descriptors identical
battle ran to its end on the host's battle service: 362 routed blocks; the host's forced switch selected its second Pokemon
both launchers report battle_finished with the original game processes, runtime objects, bridges and runtime identities
no battle ownership or pending recovery intent left; fresh terminal savers armed
the durable result is the same for both players (1v1, team 1, the friend, won; sequence 1)
each player's full personal party restored in memory (party bytes equal those before the battle)
Recent battle results on each game matches the durable result ('Battle result', 'Team 1 won')
both saved through the launcher (revision 2); parties in memory equal the canonical characters
both games closed normally, friend then host (exit codes 0, 0); save leases released
fresh launchers Continued onto the same canonical checkpoints (revision 2, same hashes as the saved mirrors)
host store integrity check passed; source saves unchanged

not_covered: 2v2, co-op Gym, wager and Championship battles
an interrupted battle (host loss, disconnect, game closed mid-battle)
physical keyboard or controller input and clicks on the launcher window (the harness calls the worker's start as the window's buttons do)
separate PCs, Wi-Fi or Internet (one machine over loopback)
